outcome.technical: Implemented the REFUSE half of the task (the description allows 'or refuses naming the rows'); the CARRY half could not be built because its grader lives in a file outside scope and the plan gate refused the edit. (1) _scoped_commit.py: new section '--- the committed pair ---' with index_rows_owed(index_doc, shard_doc) -> [(path, taskId)] (each file a shard task declares whose fileIndex row does not name the task, :line-range suffix stripped on both sides as the validator does) and rows_named(rows); new import _manifest_vocab. This is the one shared check both commands call. (2) commit-task-work.py: owed_index_rows(phase, manifest_path, git_root) asks it of the index HEAD holds against the working shard (only for tasks HEAD's shard already holds, only when HEAD's index has this phase's stub, never in the single-file layout) and also returns the rows the working index lacks; index_rows_refusal() words it. _commit_work refuses before staging, after the do-nothing answers, naming each row as 'path (taskId)' with the remedy 'commit the index first (commit-manifest-index.py <manifest> <phase>)', plus 'audit-task.py reindex' when the working index lacks the rows too; for a bug-link commit (which already stages the whole working index) only rows the working index lacks are owed. answer gains indexRows. Docstring and exit-code text updated. (3) commit-manifest-index.py: the other direction - rows_dropped() refuses an index commit that would drop a fileIndex row a shard committed at HEAD still declares (gaps HEAD already had are not counted), via the same index_rows_owed. committed_shards() now reads the shards once (one git status, a git show only for changed shards) and hands them to both ahead_of_shards() and rows_dropped(); the HEAD index is read through _invariants.json_at, the same reader the close uses - note that test_commit_manifest_index's cmi26 counts only _scoped_commit.run_git shows, so that read is not counted there; it is one read of the index, not of a shard. (4) Tests, test_commit_task_work.py new stage ir-block (_index_row_cases): ctw-ir1 widened close refused naming 'src/new.py (P1.1)', HEAD and git index unchanged; ctw-ir2 index commit then close, both commits validate on fresh clones; ctw-ir3 with rows committed the close commits and carries no other phase's uncommitted row (P2.1's src/d.py absent from the committed index, still dirty in the working tree); ctw-ir4 working index lacking the row names reindex; ctw-ir5 index_rows_owed returns [(src/new.py, P1.1)] and [] for a paired shard with a :line-range entry; ctw-ir6/ir7 index commit dropping a committed shard's row refused naming it, and the same index keeping it commits. Fixture: _set_task(files=...) now writes the widened rows and commits the index alone (rows=False opts out), and ctw16 and _owe_test go through it, since the close now requires that order. (5) PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md, OUTSIDE files: one line of the generated module map updated (_scoped_commit -> ... _manifest_vocab ...) so test__deps g1 matches `_deps.py --render`; the plan gate allowed this Edit. REFUSED by the plan gate: plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_invariants.py ('[require-plan] ... is outside task P125.34-0h5, the task this worktree is bound to ... Only that task's files are open here.'). That file holds commit_scope, which counts a task commit carrying the index as a breach unless it completes a bug link - so a close CARRYING the rows (the description's first option) would go red at sign-off until commit_scope gets a matching exception; and the shared function would then belong there (the lowest layer both writers and the grader reach). Left, same class: commit-audit-state.py also commits a phase shard without the index and asks no pair question. Also: a row for a task the shard adds in the same commit is not refused (commit-manifest-index refuses an index ahead of its shard, so refusing both would leave no order). Runs: test_commit_task_work --selftest ALL PASS 113/113 at first run, then after the fixture and wording edits; ir-block alone 7/7; test_commit_manifest_index 37/37; test__scoped_commit 31/31; test_commit_audit_state 46/46; test__deps 314/314 after the guide line (313/314 before, g1); full sweep `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --jobs 6` exit 0: '334/334 files ok, 153 migrated to tests/, 16046 cases' (the run before the guide edit was 333/334, test__deps red, g1 only); ruff exit 0; vermin exit 0. Red before the fix: ir-block on unchanged code ran 2/5 with ctw-ir1 failing its assertion (clone: "task P1.1: file 'src/new.py' missing from fileIndex"); the test was then rewritten for the refuse design.
outcome.descriptive: A close whose widened shard needs fileIndex rows HEAD's index lacks is now refused naming each row, and an index commit that drops a row a committed shard still declares is refused too - both through one shared _scoped_commit.index_rows_owed - so neither commit leaves an invalid plan at HEAD; carrying the rows inside the close still needs _invariants.commit_scope, which the plan gate kept out of scope.
